page: Microsoft Azure E96-48as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained core configuration. Based on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the system provides 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. With an x86_64 architecture supporting instruction sets like AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, it lacks support for AVX-512 extensions and AMX. The instance contains 672.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an elevated memory ratio of 14.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not provided, requiring reliance on external remote storage systems, and it does not include GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory efficiency. The instance achieved top-tier performance in the PassMark memory evaluation (3018.35) and registered strong results across multithreaded benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core (64770.05), Geekbench multi-core (16324.0), and PassMark CPU overall score (52700.88). Multithreaded bzip3 decompression and hardware encryption also perform in the top 25%. In contrast, single-thread performance benchmarks—including Geekbench single-core (1720.0) and PassMark physics testing—fall into the middle 50% category. In uncached large-block scenarios, read memory bandwidth measured 105.72 GB/sec and write bandwidth reached 58.13 GB/sec.

The constrained-core layout of this virtual machine allows workloads that are constrained by per-core software licensing to access the total 672.0 GB memory footprint of a 96-vCPU chassis while licensing only 48 vCPUs. Tradeoffs include modest large-model LLM generation speeds (2.35 tokens/sec on 70B models, falling into the bottom 10%) due to the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators or discrete GPUs. The server is well positioned for enterprise relational databases, large-scale in-memory caches, analytics engines, and data processing systems requiring high memory-per-core density.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-48as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 48 vCPUs (24 physical cores) based on the AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with 672.0 GB of memory, delivering a dense 14.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. There is no bundled local storage, discrete GPU, or complimentary public IPv4 allocation. In benchmark testing, the instance achieved top-tier marks in PassMark memory performance, backed by strong multi-core processing in stress-ng and Geekbench. Because it provides the memory volume of an E96 chassis with half the active CPU count, it presents a cost-efficient architecture for database engines constrained by per-core software licensing models. It is suitable for large in-memory databases, data analytics, and high-memory caching workloads.
